capability: An accepted run is admitted once, before destination preparation, and that admission fixes both the compilation and the processor lease it runs with (owner decision 68): a catalog or tool-configuration reload before that point ends in the existing typed pre-run refusal, shown as blocked without a new report in the UI and as exit 1 on every CLI build route; a reload after it affects only the next run; the execution catches no longer turn a non-refusal InvalidOperationException into exit 1
searchEvidence: Source read directly at 5647850c9: on the execution path, AcceptedSessionExecutionInputs.Create owns the immutable execution inputs and the live catalog check (ICanonicalCapabilityQuery.ResolveCurrentCompilation; AB authoring readiness, the AB format assessment and output naming check currency for their own results), and it ran inside AcceptedSessionCompositionExecution.ExecuteAsync after CompositionExecutionExperience had called _destinations.Prepare. CtrlRAM and AB acquired the processor lease early and compared its generation in RequireRuntimeActionReadiness, which mixed readiness-identity and runtime-generation checks in one InvalidOperationException; ExecuteCtrlRamReplaceAsync also called ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfLessThan(runtime.Generation, 1) before it, and the processor then travelled to execution as a separate parameter. ExecuteGeneralReplaceAsync acquired _acquireExternalProcessor().Processor for a plan with external-processor operations without any readiness comparison, but General Replace compiles only DP routes (BuiltInGeneralAuthoringPlanner.IsGeneralReplaceDpV2Route), so no admitted plan reaches that branch. ExternalProcessorEnvironmentLoader.AcquireCurrent returns generation 0 and a null processor once the toolchain configuration generation changes, and IsCurrent(N) turns false for an acquired generation N after a reload or a configuration change. CompositionPreRunRefusalException (APP-116-AB-PRE-RUN-REFUSAL-24, ADR 0072) was thrown only by the AB format admission; CompositionRunPresentationViewModel renders it as Preview/Build blocked without an error report, before its InvalidOperationException/IO/access/argument failed path. CliApplication.RunAsync maps requested cancellation, IO, access and argument exceptions to 70, and AbMergeCliCommandHandler caught every InvalidOperationException from execution as exit 1.

Reproduction run by the implementer (handlers called in-process, not a CLI subprocess): at cf4e42697 a tool environment reload between the CtrlRAM readiness check and execution let InvalidOperationException('Processor-backed action readiness does not match the accepted publication and runtime generation.') escape ReplaceCliCommandHandler.RunAsync, and a catalog reload after General Replace, General Merge or Standard Merge preparation let InvalidOperationException('Execution requires the exact accepted compilation to remain current.') escape the handler. That the exception then leaves CliApplication.RunAsync unhandled is from code reading; no process crash was observed. The same wrappers are the CLI regressions.

Design, revised after two R2 reviews (codex/gpt-6-astra, ACCEPT-WITH-CHANGES on v1 and v2) and owner decision 68: RunCompiledCompositionAsync acquires the processor lease of a CtrlRAM or AB run immediately before AcceptedSessionCompositionExecution.Admit, with no await in between, and Admit checks the immutable inputs, the catalog and that lease at this one admission point; the admitted run carries the inputs and the processor, and execution takes the processor only from it (second review F-1). RequireProcessorActionReadiness keeps only the readiness invariants. The lease refusal states the known fact: a different generation, no runtime after a configuration change, or an acquired generation that is no longer current (F-2). The General Replace processor branch becomes an invariant instead of an unadmitted processor acquisition, keeping processor-backed General Replace unsupported (decided point 1); readiness identity mismatch and an unavailable action stay invariants (point 2); the AB format admission keeps its own codes (point 3); ADR 0072 holds the normative rule and docs/architecture/terminal-log-and-diagnostics.md, not a governed path, only mirrors it (point 4).

Test results reported by the implementer, not independently rerun, on the proposal applied to 5647850c9: Bootstrap.Tests 1939/1939, Architecture.Tests 269/269, Application.Tests 1612/1612, GoldenRegression.Tests 14/14, UiSmoke.Tests 1672/1672; dotnet format whitespace, git diff --check and the repository Markdown link check clean. On the unchanged source 5647850c9, 15 of the 19 new or changed cases fail (Bootstrap 13 of 16, UiSmoke 2 of 3); the 4 guards pass on both (the AB format refusal, the untyped General Merge failure, the invariant priority and the UI invariant failure). On the v2 production code, exactly the two v3-specific cases fail: the equal-generation lease reports 'changed from 30 to 30', and a tool reload before the admission completes lets the run execute with the old processor.

Inference, not tested: one CLI command never reloads the catalog or tool environment on its own, so the CLI failures need a concurrent in-process change (the regressions inject it); the UI changes both while it runs (the System Information refresh reloads the catalog, the Message Center refresh reloads the tool environment, and saving a toolchain selection publishes a new tool configuration), so the UI terminal change is the one users are likely to see.

Not covered or covered only in part: the processor-backed interleavings are tested on the AB NT51950 route with a test lease source; the reload before admission completes is injected through the execution's catalog view at its first currency check, a deterministic hook that relies on the catalog check running before the lease check inside the admission; CtrlRAM is tested with reloads before execution (a new generation, and no runtime after a configuration change); the General Replace processor invariant and the self-contradictory available readiness without a positive generation are code-only; the AB CLI test covers the typed AB format refusal (AB_FORMAT_SESSION_STALE), which handles an AB catalog reload before this admission. docs/architecture/terminal-log-and-diagnostics.md gains the CLI exit-code paragraph but is not a governed path, so it is not listed in mutablePaths.
semanticOwner: AcceptedSessionCompositionExecution.Admit with AcceptedSessionExecutionInputs.Create is the single owner of accepted-run admission: at one point before destination preparation it captures the immutable inputs, requires the catalog to still publish the accepted compilation and, for CtrlRAM and AB, requires the lease acquired for that point to be the current runtime generation the readiness checked; the admitted run carries the inputs and the processor. CompositionExecutionExperience validates readiness invariants and acquires the lease at that point but decides no currency itself. CLI handlers only render the typed issues; Presentation code is unchanged.
terminalContract: ICompositionExecution.ExecuteAsync throws CompositionPreRunRefusalException with one capability.readiness.runtime-snapshot-stale issue (operation id: the session workflow) at admission, before destination preparation, output or report work, when (a) the catalog no longer publishes the accepted compilation, or (b) for a CtrlRAM or AB run the lease acquired at admission has a generation other than its valid readiness generation (reason: changed from one generation to the other), has no runtime (generation 0 after a tool-configuration change; reason: the checked runtime is no longer available), or has the readiness generation but is no longer current (reason: the acquired generation is no longer valid). A reload after admission does not affect that run, which executes with the admitted processor; the next run of the same readiness is refused. An invalid or self-contradictory request is rejected first as InvalidOperationException; a General Replace plan with external-processor operations is rejected as an invariant; owners that check currency earlier keep their own refusal issues (the AB format admission's, for example AB_FORMAT_SESSION_STALE). CLI: standard-merge, general-merge, ctrlram-replace and general-replace print 'Issues:' with the refusal and exit 1 (for standard-merge a new explicit classification; its other exit-70 failures are unchanged); ab-merge prints 'error: <message>' and exits 1 for the refusal only. A non-refusal InvalidOperationException from the execution call is not turned into exit 1 by these new or narrowed catches; the existing outer mappings, such as CliApplication.RunAsync returning 70 for cancellation, IO, access and argument exceptions, are unchanged. UI: Preview or Build blocked with the issue code and message and 'No output', no new report, the loaded report and report history unchanged; the other handled failures keep the failed path and its error report.

designReview.evidence: The v1 (base c7982652179f20d49a0b38f51dfc2c82c8146c22) and v2 (patch SHA-256 a4ce1f55a5fc62fcac13359436866f746f8258c435ee5f359d7ebfc44c78e40e, base 5647850c912ce1460caf66b8dc71ac286f922154) proposals received ACCEPT-WITH-CHANGES from codex/gpt-6-astra, and their findings F-1 to F-6 are incorporated in v3. Independent R2 design re-review by codex/gpt-6-astra of CLI-EXEC-REFUSAL-1113-01 v3, implemented by claude-code. Reviewed proposal patch SHA-256 3364f934d20d49f908ea1c6a0ff4d20a2bfb474cca31272e5f6a7fbea9721a8c against base 5647850c912ce1460caf66b8dc71ac286f922154. F-1, F-2 and F-6 are closed. Admit/Create jointly own accepted-run admission before destination preparation, and execution consumes the admitted compilation, immutable inputs and processor without reacquisition. Lease acquisition followed by catalog observation and final lease validation establishes a common admission point under the production loaders’ monotonic generation semantics. Decision 68, refusal classifications, CLI/UI terminal behavior and record scope are consistent. The disclosed test limitations do not block design admission. Patch applicability was checked; no files were modified and no builds or tests were run. Test results remain implementer-reported. ACCEPT for design admission; final implementation and integration gates remain outstanding.
